/-!
# Conjecture 9.51

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$ in the free
group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. It is modelled here as `PresentedGroup rels` for a
`Finset` `rels` of elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`.

The word problem of a finitely presented group $G = \langle X \mid R \rangle$
asks for an algorithm deciding whether a word in the generators and their
inverses represents the identity of $G$. Solubility of the word problem does
not depend on the chosen finite presentation, so it can be tested on the
presentation defining the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      WellFoundedGT
        {N : Subgroup (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) // N.Normal} ∧
      ¬ ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) ↦
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

Here a group $G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ with $R$ finite is

* *soluble* if its derived series reaches the trivial subgroup (`IsSolvable`);
* satisfying the *maximum condition on normal subgroups* (max-$n$) if every
  ascending chain of normal subgroups of $G$ is eventually constant, i.e. the
  poset of normal subgroups of $G$ is well-founded for $>$ (`WellFoundedGT`);
* of *insoluble word problem* if there is no algorithm deciding, for a word
  $w \in (X \cup X^{-1})^*$ in the generators and their inverses (a
  `List (Fin n × Bool)`, where `(i, true)` is $x_i$ and `(i, false)` is
  $x_i^{-1}$), whether the image of $w$ in $G$ is the identity
  (`¬ ComputablePred`).

@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no existence question (Prop: ∃ G, finitely presented ∧ solvable ∧ max-n ∧ word problem undecidable), to be stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ …`; subtleties: 'soluble' = solvable group, 'maximum condition on normal subgroups' (max-n) = every ascending chain of normal subgroups stabilises (equivalently every normal subgroup is finitely generated as a normal subgroup, a well-founded/`WellFoundedGT` condition on the lattice of normal subgroups), 'insoluble word problem' = undecidable (non-computable) word problem, a property independent of the chosen finite presentation, and 'con-\linebreak dition' is just a hyphenation artifact for 'condition'.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and encode the same mathematics: ∃ n, ∃ finite relator set in FreeGroup (Fin n) with PresentedGroup soluble (IsSolvable), max-n (WellFoundedGT on {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal}, whose < is strict inclusion — verified by Iff.rfl — so this is exactly the ascending chain condition via wellFoundedGT_iff_monotone_chain_condition), and ¬ComputablePred for the predicate 'word w : List (Fin n × Bool) maps to 1' (FreeGroup.mk uses (i,false) for inverses; Primcodable instance exists). The direct PresentedGroup formulation (c01, c05–c08) is chosen over the bespoke-definition versions (c03, c04) and the ≃*-witness version (c02) because it is simplest and needs no new definitions; these are all equivalent since solubility/max-n are isomorphism invariants and word-problem decidability is independent of the finite presentation. c07's declaration shape (Finset relators) was taken, with c01's fuller docstring and AMS 3 20 tags. Boundary check: n = 0 (or any presentation of the trivial group) has computable word problem (verified in a scratch file), so the existential has no degenerate witness; answer(True) = positive answer.

@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔

      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧

items: A finitely presented group is represented directly as `PresentedGroup` on generators `Fin n` with a finite relator set `r : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))`; quantifying over `n` and `r` ranges over finite presentations up to group isomorphism.
The maximum condition on normal subgroups is encoded as `WellFoundedGT` on the subtype of normal subgroups ordered by inclusion, equivalently the ascending chain condition.

The word problem is the identity predicate for the canonical map from finite lists of signed generators into the presented group. Its insolubility is encoded as the negation of `ComputablePred`. Using raw finite words rather than quotient free-group elements supplies Mathlib's canonical `Primcodable` input type and is equivalent to the standard word problem.

reviewer_notes: Single yes/no existence question; no ambiguity in the source beyond the 'con-\linebreak dition' hyphenation artifact. Modeling choices: 'soluble' = Mathlib IsSolvable; 'maximum condition on normal subgroups' = WellFoundedGT on the subtype of normal subgroups (ACC); 'insoluble word problem' = ¬ComputablePred on raw signed words, using Mathlib's Nat.Partrec-based computability with the standard Primcodable encoding (encoding-independent up to computable bijection). Quantifying over concrete PresentedGroup (Fin n) rels rather than an abstract G is faithful because every finitely presented group is isomorphic to such a group and all three properties are presentation-independent. c03's ∀-over-generating-families and c04's ∃-over-generating-families word-problem definitions are also correct for f.p. groups but add unnecessary bespoke definitions. No slot omitted.
